_comment: The single place the native apps get their identity from. Read by capacitor.config.ts, by android/app/build.gradle, and by scripts/mobile-identity.mjs, so an identifier can never be right in one project and wrong in the other. NOT YET REGISTERED with either store — see `registered` below.
_appName_comment: The name that appears under the icon on a phone's home screen, and nowhere else. It is title-cased — Hangyul Ganada — because a launcher label sits beside Photos, Maps and Settings, and a lowercased second word reads there as a typo rather than as the deliberate lowercase of 가나다. The prose product name in the app, the store listing and every document stays `Hangyul ganada`; scripts/check-product-name.mjs enforces that split, and scripts/check-mobile-identity.mjs enforces that Android's strings.xml and iOS's Info.plist both carry exactly this value. Changing the name here and nowhere else is the supported way to rename the installed app.

registered._comment: Set each to true only once the identifier has actually been created in the corresponding console. Nothing in the build depends on these; they exist so the release checklist cannot be answered from memory.

_version_comment: 1.0.6. Moved up from 1.0.5 because this release changes what a learner reads: twenty-three taught words were retired under the child-safe content policy (docs/CHILD_SAFE_CONTENT_POLICY.md) — 살인, 무기, 총알, 미사일, 전쟁, 죽이다, 취하다, 벌거벗다 and fifteen more — one example sentence was rewritten with its thirty-one translations and two new recordings, the searchable dictionary lost 694 headwords and 525 senses the policy refuses, and the Level Test bank, the daily gap-fills and the audio manifest were regenerated from the corrected corpus. What a customer would notice: the course teaches 3,370 words rather than 3,393, and a placement question can no longer offer 섹스하다 as a choice, which one did. Nothing has been uploaded to either console — see `registered` — so no listing has to be explained.
_buildNumber_comment: 24, because 23 is spent. The delivered APK and AAB both report versionCode 23 and product files have changed since: the content-safety policy, the builders that read it, the runtime gate that revalidates a bank on load, and every generated content file. A code that has been used by a set of bytes is not reused for different bytes; `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` said so before this build rather than after, which is what I-152 exists for.

android._comment: targetSdk 36 because Google Play requires Android 16 for new apps and updates from 31 August 2026. minSdk 24 is Capacitor 8's floor and covers ~99% of active devices.

xcode._comment: What `App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` currently carries, written down here so that a check can tell a *deliberate lag* from a *drift*. The Xcode project is maintained on a Mac, by hand, through the Xcode UI: MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION are build settings Xcode owns, and editing them from Linux with a text substitution is how a project file loses a setting it was never asked about. So this release moves Android to 1.0.6 build 24 and leaves iOS where its maintainer left it. `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` asserts the project file matches these two values exactly — any other change to it fails — and prints the pending action while they are behind `version` and `buildNumber`.
xcode.pending: iOS is behind: set MARKETING_VERSION to 1.0.6 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION to 24 in Xcode (App target, both configurations), then update the two values above in the same commit. The project file is not edited from here — see the comment above.

ios._comment: 15.0 to match IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in the Xcode project — the two disagreeing is how a build succeeds and then crashes on a device the store said it supported. Capacitor 8's own floor is 14; 15 is chosen because it is what the project is configured for and covers every device Apple still updates. Apple requires builds made with the iOS 26 SDK from 28 April 2026; that is the SDK you build *with*, not the version you deploy *to*.
